articles.title: ESPHome adds wired control for Airton air conditioners
articles.dek: An ESP board can replace the original Wi-Fi module, giving compatible units direct climate controls and extra settings.
body: ESPHome adds direct serial control for Airton air conditioners that use a connection to their original Wi-Fi module. An ESP board replaces that module and talks to the air conditioner, providing a wired alternative to ESPHome’s existing Airton infrared control.

The component combines climate control with switches for the display, ionizer, health, sleep and eco settings, plus readings for total usage time and protocol revision. Guillaume DELVIT makes his first contribution to ESPHome with the addition, tested on ESP32.

pullRequests.title: [airton_serial] Add Airton serial climate component
[airton_serial] Add Airton Serial Climate documentation

articles.title: Music Assistant brings Qobuz’s album selections to Discover
articles.dek: Seven collections bring editorial picks, new releases and popular albums into one browsing page.
body: Music Assistant adds Qobuz’s album selections to its Discover page. Seven rows cover new releases, best sellers, most-streamed albums, press awards, editor’s picks, Qobuzissime and Ideal Discography.
These are Qobuz’s global selections rather than recommendations tailored to an individual account. Robin Fourcade makes his first contribution to Music Assistant’s server with the addition.

pullRequests.title: Show Qobuz editorial album lists as Discover recommendation rows

media.alt: Music Assistant Discover page showing Qobuz album recommendation rows.

articles.title: ESPHome reads presence and 3D positions from LD6004 radar
articles.dek: The Hi-Link sensor reports up to three targets, including their position in space.
body: ESPHome adds support for the Hi-Link LD6004 radar, exposing presence and the three-dimensional positions of up to three detected targets. Makers can use overall presence, individual target presence and detection-area presence in their automations.

Readings include target count and each target’s X, Y and Z coordinates. Rick van Hattem makes his first contribution to ESPHome with the shared radar parser supporting this work, alongside the LD6004 component.

pullRequests.title: [ld600x] Add shared TinyFrame parser and use it in ld6002b
[ld6004] Add Hi-Link LD6004 radar with binary_sensor platform
[ld6004] Add sensor platform

articles.title: ESPHome stops weekend schedules running every day
articles.dek: Schedules crossing the end of a week or day keep to their intended range, including overnight hours.
body: ESPHome corrects schedules whose ranges wrap around the end of a day or week. A Saturday-to-Sunday range previously matched every day, while an hour range from 22 to 2 matched all 24 hours. They now select the intended weekend or late-night hours.

Related validation rejects impossible range endpoints and invalid repetition steps before a device is built. That prevents malformed schedules from either crashing validation or silently never firing.

pullRequests.title: [time] Fix cron ranges wrapping around the end of the scale
[time] Reject invalid '/' step and offset in cron expressions

articles.title: ESPHome updates Nordic devices across the network
articles.dek: Compatible nRF52 devices gain an upload path over IP, including Thread networks.
body: ESPHome adds network firmware updates for nRF52 devices using its Zephyr update service. A configured device can receive firmware by IP address or hostname, including over Thread, through the normal command-line upload process.

Ardumine adds the network transport alongside the existing update paths. The update process checks that an image fits the available update space and refuses another upload while a previous update is still pending.

pullRequests.title: [zephyr_mcumgr] Add SMP UDP  OTA transport for nRF52
[zephyr_mcumgr] Document the SMP over UDP OTA transport

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps Android dashboards visible to screen readers
articles.dek: An embedded browser race could hide the whole panel from assistive technology while it looked normal.
body: Home Assistant corrects an Android dashboard failure that could leave screen readers with no panel to navigate even though the page looked normal. The problem affects the older frontend build used in Android’s embedded browser.
Maarten Lakerveld changes how the page establishes its background layer, avoiding the timing problem that could hide the panel from assistive technology. The dashboard keeps the same appearance.

pullRequests.title: Move the panel background stacking context off partial-panel-resolver

articles.title: Home Assistant puts a parked Škoda on the map
articles.dek: The car’s parking position becomes a tracker when the vehicle supplies coordinates.
body: Home Assistant adds a map location for a parked Škoda. The tracker uses the parking coordinates already returned with the vehicle’s data, without making extra requests to the car service.

The tracker only appears for vehicles that report a parking position. It becomes unknown while the car is driving and the service provides no coordinates, so this is a parked-car locator rather than a live journey tracker. Philipp Ballhausen makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the addition.

pullRequests.title: Add parking position device tracker to Škoda

articles.title: Home Assistant bypasses incorrect read-only labels in myUplink
articles.dek: A direct action lets heating automations submit writable settings that the service describes incorrectly.
body: Home Assistant adds a direct myUplink action for settings that the service incorrectly describes as read-only. A writable zone temperature target can otherwise appear only as a sensor; the new action lets an automation submit its value directly.
Åke Strandberg keeps the service’s own checks in place: myUplink must still accept the change, and a refused write produces an error.

pullRequests.title: Add set_datapoint action to myuplink

articles.title: Home Assistant gives spoken feedback when picker searches change
articles.dek: Screen readers receive the search text and result count after a short pause in typing.
body: Home Assistant adds spoken feedback to search pickers so a screen-reader user can tell when a query has changed the list. After a short pause in typing, the picker announces the search text and matching result count, including when there are no matches.
The count excludes section headings and permanent actions such as adding a custom item. Chanelle makes her first contribution to the Home Assistant frontend with the change.

pullRequests.title: Announce the number of search results in pickers

articles.title: Piper helps voice builders spot unfinished training
articles.dek: New diagnostics and dependable checkpoints make long voice-training runs easier to assess.
body: Piper gives people building local speech voices clearer signs that a training run has not finished learning. A reconstruction check examines the sound-generating model separately, and a warning flags runs exposed to too little speech.

Each completed training round also saves the latest checkpoint, even when its score misses the five best results. Michael Hansen’s expanded guide explains how to assess training duration and voice-quality scores, which vary by language and do not judge pronunciation.

pullRequests.title: Training diagnostics, a per-epoch last.ckpt, and docs on val_mos and run length

articles.title: Home Assistant follows covers moved outside its own controls
articles.dek: Overkiz tracks commands started in apps such as TaHoma, keeping movement and cancellation in sync.
body: Home Assistant follows Overkiz cover commands started elsewhere, including in the TaHoma app. A blind or shutter moving through those controls can show that it is opening or closing in Home Assistant, instead of appearing idle.
The integration follows the external command until it finishes or fails, and its existing cancellation handling can recognize that movement too.

pullRequests.title: Track Overkiz executions started outside Home Assistant

articles.title: ESPHome repairs MQTT date and time controls
articles.dek: Home Assistant can interpret the device’s values and send changes back in the expected format.
body: ESPHome repairs the MQTT discovery information for date, time and combined date-and-time controls. Home Assistant previously left their states unknown and sent commands the device could not parse; the added conversion templates translate both directions.
The existing JSON messages on the MQTT topics stay unchanged for other clients and automations. Combined date-and-time values assume the ESPHome device and Home Assistant use the same timezone.

articles.title: Mac scripts adjust Music Assistant’s selected speaker
articles.dek: Volume commands follow the chosen local or remote player rather than only the computer’s output.
body: Music Assistant connects its selected-player volume controls to the desktop app’s AppleScript interface on macOS. Scripts can set or change the volume of the selected local or remote player alongside the existing playback commands.

David Bishop’s frontend work completes the matching desktop support added earlier in the week. Requests handle missing players and timeouts without leaving the application unresponsive; the addition does not change the player’s on-screen controls.

pullRequests.title: Expose selected-player volume commands to the companion app
feat(macos): control selected player volume through scripting

articles.title: Z-Wave JS protects unrelated files during configuration updates
articles.dek: An incorrectly chosen external configuration folder is no longer cleared indiscriminately.
body: Z-Wave JS stops clearing an external configuration folder unless it is empty or contains the project’s version marker. That protects unrelated files when an installation points its external configuration setting at the wrong non-empty folder.
Configuration downloads also gain a decompression limit and checks that keep extracted files inside the intended directory.

pullRequests.title: fix: harden config updates and config file parsing

articles.title: ESPHome restores LibreTiny builds in its Mac app
articles.dek: A space in the app’s Python installation path no longer stops compatible device builds.
body: ESPHome fixes LibreTiny builds on Apple Silicon Macs when its Python installation lives in a path containing spaces, as it does in the ESPHome Builder app. The failure stopped builds for BK72xx, RTL87xx and LN882x devices before firmware could be produced.
The correction preserves the full installation path when starting the compiler. It was verified with a BK7231N build in the affected application location.
